source.display_title: 05/26/2026 - Jorge Fernández  x Andrew Musial  — Lost

setter.evidence: No KFS/KL/DH suffix in the title and no setter named. The lead came from an Instagram ad that the prospect did not seek out — 'Instagram, I don't remember the name of the guy. Trevor. Maybe, I don't know... it popped up' — and he was not a follower. Whoever booked it set no expectation whatsoever: he opened the call with 'I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know what this is, actually.'

prospect.name: Jorge Fernández
prospect.location: Mexican; currently three months into a family trip through Europe, in Italy at the time of the call, staying rent-free in his wife's aunt's house; returning to Mexico in two months
prospect.occupation: Not established. He self-identifies as a business owner or operator — 'I understand the way this works, I do this for a living as well' and 'you're a businessman, I'm a business guy too' — and says 'I work a lot', but the rep never asked what he actually does. The 'Tualo' suffix on his Zoom label suggests a company affiliation, unverified on the call.
prospect.family_status: Married, travelling with his wife and two daughters aged three and one. His father is 75 and, in his words, 'looks 95' and is 'a crippled old guy' who never exercised. His father-in-law is the same age, exercises a lot, and is 'amazing'. The contrast is his stated motivator.
prospect.training_background: Effectively none. 'I've never been in a good shape, ever' and 'I've never, ever done any exercise', no sport ever played. Three prior attempts, each abandoned at roughly two weeks: a high-school programme with a friend, a gym routine plus a nutritionist, and a Better Me app subscription restarted when his first child was born. Currently three weeks into self-directed YouTube calisthenics at home, around 30 minutes a session — the longest streak of his life.

signals: Anchored to a cheaper alternative that is genuinely working: three weeks of free YouTube calisthenics, the longest he has ever sustained anything, and he said so as an explicit head-to-head — 'if we compare them, they're both at home. Amazing. They're both easy and quick. Amazing... But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest.'

Self-directed by choice and by constraint: 'The reason why I've been training the last three weeks and I'm planning to do it by myself is because I don't have the budget to pay somebody to follow me.'

Explicitly conceded the value and still refused the price, which is the signature of this avatar rather than a value objection — he agreed the coaching layer works ('Definitely. I definitely agree') and bought none of it.

Wants a cheap way to test commitment before committing capital, stated as a fully worked analogy: 'I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then ride it a bit, and then see if I really like it, and then see if that's really a priority... and after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.'

COUNTER-SIGNAL: he is not price-shopping a market — he had no competing quote and no idea of the price band ('Sounds expensive. That's what I'm waiting to hear'). His reference point for a fitness purchase is a $25 tub of protein powder. He is closer to a non-buyer than a bargain hunter, and 'other / never_bought_fitness' was considered; skeptical_bargain_hunter was kept because the free-alternative comparison drove the whole decision.

goals.text: Build muscle and see a visible physical change within the three-month travel window — 'I decided that I wanted to use this three-month travel to build muscle and exercise'
Prove to himself he can look good — 'One is to prove myself that I can look better and be better. Look at myself in the mirror and say, hey, I can do this'
Make a better impression physically — 'whenever somebody looks at me, I'll make a better impression regarding my physique'

Be healthier and push back the onset of age-related decline — 'increasing the chances that health issues don't arise as soon, and that my crippling regarding old age down the road extends as much as possible'
Not end up like his father, who is 75, 'looks 95' and never exercised — and to end up like his father-in-law, the same age and 'amazing', who does
Be able to keep up with two daughters aged three and one — 'They make me exercise even if I don't want to'
Get the best shape of his life now, before it gets harder — 'if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday... I'll die never having seen what that could have been like'
Train mobility and movement, not just muscle — the specific thing that made him take the call

pains.text: Three prior attempts, all abandoned at about two weeks — high school programme, gym plus nutritionist, and the Better Me app restarted when his first child was born
Does not enjoy training enough to prioritise it — 'It's that I don't like it enough. So not to make it into my schedule, definitely. I'd rather watch a TV series than work out'

No idea whether he is executing movements correctly — 'I do a push-up, and I'm thinking, like, damn, I have no idea if I did this push-up the right way or not... I feel like I'm doing it but I'm not sure'
Nobody correcting or following him up — 'if there was somebody standing right next to me telling me like, hey, no, those legs aren't straight, I'd be correcting them, but I don't have it'
Works a lot and would rather spend spare time with his family than in a gym — 'I've always said that I have no time to exercise, because it's something that takes a lot of time'
Acute awareness that the window is closing at 34 — 'I'm starting in a point of my life where I'm going down, regarding my best physical age'
Very lean ectomorph who has held the same weight since he was 15 and has never been able to build — 'no matter how much I eat, I'll never... I've been having the same weight since I was 15'
Dislikes gyms outright, which rules out the conventional route — 'going to the gym, for me, it's like, it doesn't make sense for me, at least. And I respect it, but I don't like it'
No liquid cash — travelling, credit cards already committed to flights, no budget for coaching of any kind

objections.raw_quote: Sounds expensive. That's what I'm waiting to hear.
objections.rep_response: Did not address the price signal at all. He ran the pre-close belief question instead ('If you had the right training, a simple nutrition, and someone like Trevor in your corner... would you agree that you would get to your goal?'), got a yes, and moved to explaining delivery. The prospect had to interrupt the onboarding logistics to force the number out: 'Before that, I'd like to understand the full picture. It sounds expensive.'

objections.raw_quote: I don't think it's something I can afford. But I don't know what would be the next step. Like, for me to think about it and give you an answer? Or how does it go?
objections.rep_response: Refused the drift to a think-about-it and isolated immediately — 'finances aside, are you 100% sure that you can actually achieve your goals with Trevor?' then 'Is there anything else holding you back?' He then pushed on what 'no money' actually meant ('you're a businessman, I'm a business guy too... you don't have the full amount?'), got permission for an open financial conversation, and took a partial financial picture: liquid cash (zero), credit card usage, credit score. He offered a financing partner. He did not ask monthly surplus after bills, how many cards, available credit per card, used versus available, or investments — which are the questions that would have determined whether financing was actually viable for someone with zero cash.

objections.raw_quote: if we compare them, they're both at home. Amazing. They're both easy and quick. Amazing. They both give you more strength. Amazing. One of them also gives you the mobility and that sounds super amazing. One of them also has somebody that's following you up and giving you personal assistance and motivation and personalizing the training and the nutrition and whatever. Super amazing. That sounds amazing. But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest. I'm going to be honest.
objections.rep_response: Improvised, and largely conceded the ground. He agreed the content is free — 'Everything, all the knowledge, everything, it's on YouTube. You can look it up' — which handed the prospect his own argument ('Yeah, that's exactly my point'). He then made the only correct move available, differentiating on accountability and programming: 'the difference is in the accountability, especially' and 'if you haven't been like a gym rat or working out for 10 years, setting up a proper plan...'. The prospect fully agreed with the differentiation and still would not pay. There is no scripted play for this objection.

objections.raw_quote: if I was, like, a year into it, and I knew this was something I was really invested in, it's like, I don't know, wanting to starting to learn how to bike, and after two seconds, going and buying a mountain bike that's 6k. I would never do that. I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with it and closed the call out: 'Yeah, yeah, makes sense. Look, maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes.' Objection D was not run in any form. Notably, the prospect had himself argued the exact opposite thirty-five minutes earlier — 'every day that passes from now on, it's harder, not easier... if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday' — and the rep did not use it.

objections.raw_quote: As I told you before, I don't know if specifically Trevor, but like you said, if there's...
objections.rep_response: Glossed over it. The rep treated the answer as a yes and moved straight to 'so we're not talking about the money is the only obstacle right now from proceeding.' The prospect had just said he could not distinguish this coach from any competent coach, which is a live differentiation problem and, strictly, means the isolation was never cleanly achieved.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structured plan. The rep stated 'we don't have anything set in stone, like payment plans, but if there's a will, there's a way' and then offered a third-party financing partner. No amounts, terms or schedule were named, and the prospect declined the concept outright.

prospect_financials.disclosure_notes: Verbatim on cash: 'my current cash is zero... I have the exact cash I need to pay my credit cards, which I've used to buy the tickets to fly to Italy. So yeah, zero.' He uses credit cards but available versus used credit was never asked. Asked for his credit score he answered 'Amazing. 10.', which is not a value on any standard credit-score scale and was not clarified — credit_score recorded as null rather than guessed. Also disclosed: no rent while travelling (staying in his wife's aunt's house), and heavy discretionary spend on food in Italy.

evidence: Explicit refusal of the offer and of financing: 'So, for 6k? No. Because it's not something I would ever pay 6k for.'

The rep disqualified rather than discounted, and said so: 'Look, maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes.' The prospect accepted it — 'Everything sounds amazing, but I knew it was something that was gonna be difficult... I suspected that was the case.'
Parted cleanly with no next step, no follow-up call, and no artifact to send: 'no hard feelings, like I said at the beginning. If it's alignment, it's cool. If not, no worries.'

The prospect had conceded the value entirely before refusing, which makes this a pure affordability and priority loss rather than a value loss: 'That would definitely improve my chances of getting there. As you just said, the equation sounds amazing. But there's a fourth ingredient there. That's the money.'

He also self-disqualified on priority under questioning, which the rep drew out well: 'I pay Netflix, because I love movies. And I pay delicious food... But that's a priority for me. My physique... not that much.'

Counter-evidence worth recording: intent was real and current, not theoretical — three weeks into self-directed training, the longest streak of his life, protein and creatine bought that week, and an articulate motivational stack around his father's decline and two young daughters. This was a genuinely motivated prospect with zero money.
outcome.next_step: None. Call ended as a mutual, amicable disqualification with no follow-up scheduled and nothing sent.

notable.note: The cleanest disqualification in the batch and, on process, one of the better-run calls — but it exposes three things worth escalating. (1) FUNNEL, not rep: the prospect arrived from an Instagram ad he had not sought out, was not a follower of Trevor, and opened with 'I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know what this is, actually.' Nobody set an expectation of price, format or seriousness before the call. Forty-three minutes of a closer's time went to someone with zero liquid cash whose reference point for a fitness purchase is a $25 tub of protein powder. That is a targeting and qualification problem upstream. (2) The free-alternative objection now has its extreme case on record. The known script gap was written around a $29/month coach; here the competing product costs nothing, is currently working, and the prospect built the comparison himself, feature by feature, conceding every point of superiority and still choosing free. The rep's only counter — accountability and programming — was agreed with and did not move him. (3) The single biggest coaching miss is a gift the rep left on the table: at 00:07:28 Jorge argued the Objection D rebuttal himself, unprompted — 'if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday' — and at 00:41:21, when he said 'after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now', the rep agreed with him instead of quoting his own words back. Separately: the rep asked for a credit score and accepted 'Amazing. 10.' as an answer, then offered financing on that basis. Pricing was quoted correctly at $6,000 for six months on this call — worth contrasting with the $4,000 three-month tier the same rep quoted the previous day.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout; roles read from content. Clear examples: at 00:04:21 'It's called ectomorph' is attributed to the prospect but is obviously the rep supplying the term, and the height exchange immediately after is inverted so that 'And how tall are you?' sits under the prospect's label; at 00:10:23 'Three and one' (the daughters' ages) sits under the rep's label but is the prospect's answer; the entire block from roughly 00:37:00 to 00:38:00 runs as one undifferentiated paragraph under a single label containing both sides of the exchange; and at 00:41:00-00:41:09 the credit-card and credit-score questions and answers are swapped, so 'what's your credit score?' lands under the prospect and 'Amazing. 10.' lands under him too. There is also a ~2.5 minute gap at the start (00:00:15 to 00:02:39) with connection setup, and a freeze around 00:32:24. Several passages contain untranscribable ASR garbage ('lost lost Spebaum No the And But And', '과どう they with What What What's What'). The rep's display label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the title and folder say Andrew Musial; recorded as Andrew Musial, flagged for confirmation.
